title: Joining George Lewis for the West Coast after Joe Watkins leaves
summary: Frazier replaces Joe Watkins, goes by train to San Francisco, plays the Jazz Jubilee in Los Angeles, and hears complaints about Watkins.

story.theme_name: Going west: California and the Los Angeles scene
story.community_name: Going west: moving to and working in California

blocks.x: I was going to ask you, do you remember when Joe Walken came back into the Lewis band when you was out in the West Coast? Was it?
I put him back in the band. Yeah.

Well, he was working out in San Francisco with a man called King Guglio and Earl Hans. And I guess they didn't like his style because how that all started, they was working, during that time, the whole band was working at the paddock. Which band?
George Lewis band. You see? And George had some bookings to go out to the West. George's band is famous on the West Coast.

All I can know is the West Coast. And he know the band already going to have a booking to go out there. But some fellas, you see, they get head swollen like that and they say they're not used to experience traveling. And when this, Earl Hans, that was a man who had what you call original. He was, we know he come from big bands out of Chicago. You would call them swing bands, you understand? That, I know that. Seen him and I heard him. And they form a band, a Dixieland group in San Francisco. And when they sent down here to get New Orleans jazz drumming, they do that sometimes. Mixing fellas. That's how they did Freda Coleman. They brought in foot with this big fine band in California. That big, I forget that. There's a white outfit. I forget them guys' names. But they just use him as a Dixieland man. Because he's good at drumming and playing with the big band. You could do that, but you see, a drummer can make a swing or a jazz. If you got a jazz drummer, you can take any, take five minutes out of the big band and you can make them play Dixieland style. I know I can do that with any big band. The way you play, you make them play that way. So, Freda did that, but he just had a month's work to do that. But Joe Watson went up with King Gurley and Earl Hans, them fellas. And then, that's why I understand why he wanted to quit. He's band at the paddock. He knew his band was going up there. You see? So, they all started warning me, ringing me at 2 o'clock in the morning. I was living on Arbor Street there. Well, Lawrence called me, my cousin. They asked me, George said, I said, sure, I play with George. I ain't doing nothing but the Spartan. So, he said, well, come at the paddock. They got two more weeks at the paddock before they go to California. Well, they said two weeks in a few days. Well, I went and started playing with Joe. He said, well, after Joe Watson left, because he had to ship off and go away to San Francisco. Well, I went to work for the men's to finish that job up. And then, we left here on a Sunday. And that Saturday night before we left, Lawrence suffered a stroke. Oh, yeah. You see? And that was it. And then, how we left that Sunday morning to go to San Francisco. We got to San Francisco that Tuesday at 1.30. We left here that Sunday morning, by railroad. And we played up there. And after we had, see, we had two weeks working in San Francisco, and three months, job in Los Angeles. But the Saturday morning we left San Francisco to come down to Los Angeles, every year in October they had what they called a Jazz Jubilee. Yeah. Big concert with bands all over the United States. Oh, yeah, that's Frank Gold. Yeah, that piece in the Coliseum and all bands take part in that. Yeah. Well, I met men up there. I ain't met in many years like Kid Ory, minor Hall and all them people. I ain't seen any musicians in years. Well, by being with George, when we left Frisco that morning, well, the same morning we was leaving France, San Francisco to come down to Los Angeles. It takes a train ten hours to run that. That's 481 miles by railroad. And we had to be at that. Well, we can make a train leave about eight something and get in Los Angeles, about six something in the evening. Concerts don't start until about 8 or 8.30 that night, you see. And then you got nine bands. Each band played half an hour. No. So we had plenty of time, you know. Then you'd have fellas that meet you with cabs and automobiles to bring you to the Coliseum or the tour. But I mean, that night, I mean that morning, that's where George told us that the fellas was kicking on Joe Watson. They don't like he can solo or something. I didn't worry about going to the Coliseum. We had nights off in San Francisco, but I didn't worry about going down there by the hangover where they was playing. I used to stay around the rooming house. And they wanted me to go. I said, I don't want to go. I don't feel like going. When I first got to Frisco, I was staying in the rooming house. So I got the man where we stopped. I knew them from here, the old man Jackson. They used to live on Burgundy in St. Peter. And people went up there during the wars and they accumulated a little money and they got their own rooming house, you see. And we used to sit down and talk. When we got there that Tuesday, we didn't have to go to work until that Friday, you see, of the same week and play that Friday Saturday. Then the next week we'd play a study from that Monday clean up to that Friday and then leave that Saturday and come to Los Angeles.
How come that Joe got back into the band and you left?

Then, yeah, when I came to Los Angeles, that's why George Lewis told us that they was, they put a, give him a two weeks notice, but I'd play, just pay in advance. That's the union laws. Yeah. So, Joe, King Goodall, try to help but, Earl Hines did that. So we left that morning and that's the same morning that happened to Joe Watkins, because he was living at the hangover club with George Lewis while we was in San Francisco. So when we go down to Los Angeles playing down there, he, well a few days after we was in Los Angeles, he came by there, you see. I mean a week after we was there and he came a few days after we played the first week and he was on his way home, you see. So I say whatever George put him back George didn't want with him mad since he quit the band now, you see. I say, well I'm going on back to New Orleans. New Orleans, but it's been like it is now. Like I had all my daughters out of Finn, but they didn't want me to go to all the people that liked it, because the first time I played in that place, I met.
